name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX-1)
key_phenomenon: Symmetrical spherical diffusion flame envelope; classic d-squared law droplet regression.
detection_challenge: No convective plume; thermal sensors must be in close proximity to droplet tether.
extinction_mechanism: Radiative loss exceeded chemical heat release; tested CO2 and Helium dilution suppression.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Droplet fires without ventilation self-extinguish faster due to build-up of combustion products (CO2/H2O) around flame sphere.

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2 (FLEX-2)
key_phenomenon: Discovery of quasi-steady low-temperature 'cool flames' (~600 K) persisting invisibly after hot flame extinction.
detection_challenge: Total lack of visible radiation; optical smoke & standard flame detectors register false-negative extinction.
extinction_mechanism: Two-stage extinction: hot flame terminates via radiation, cool flame sustains via low-T alkylperoxy kinetics.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Post-fire procedures MUST enforce a minimum 45-minute cabin isolation before restoring air circulation to prevent explosive reignition.

name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
hardware_facility: MSG - Modular Flow Duct & Aerosol Sensor Suite
fuel_name: Pyrolyzed Teflon, Kapton, Cotton, Silicone Rubber
key_phenomenon: Generated typical spacecraft overheat smoke particles to calibrate ISS smoke sensors under zero-convection conditions.
detection_challenge: Microgravity smoke particles agglomerate into significantly larger, slower-moving soot chains than on Earth, altering optical scattering.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Ionization detectors lose sensitivity by up to 50% for larger microgravity smoke agglomerates; optical obscuration detectors require tailored calibration.

name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT)
hardware_facility: ISS Ambient Cabin Atmosphere (Handheld SAME Sensors)
fuel_name: Ambient Spacecraft Dust (Skin flakes, clothing lint, launch debris)
key_phenomenon: Quantified background aerosol dust loading to prevent false smoke alarms during crew exercise and vacuum filter changes.
detection_challenge: High concentrations of floating skin cells and fabric fibers trigger nuisance false fire alarms on standard optical smoke sensors.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Spacecraft smoke alarms must employ multi-angle scattering or dual-wavelength IR to discriminate real carbon smoke from cabin dust (Artemis II alarm lesson).

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment I (Large Scale)
key_phenomenon: First large-scale (0.4m x 1.0m) fire test in an uncrewed spacecraft; upward convective air current of 20 cm/s.
detection_challenge: Massive delayed carbon monoxide (CO) spike occurred well before optical smoke detectors registered obscuration.
extinction_mechanism: Fuel consumed down to fiberglass scaffold; flame front self-limited by available air flow.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Small laboratory tests underestimate large-scale spacecraft fire growth rates by up to 2.5x.

name: Saffire-IV (Artemis Lunar Exploration Atmosphere)
fuel_name: Sibal, PMMA, Nomex, Combustion Clean-up filter
key_phenomenon: Tested elevated oxygen (26% O2) and reduced pressure (55 kPa) simulating Artemis Lunar Gateway habitat.
detection_challenge: Elevated oxygen drastically accelerated ignition delay times (<1.5 seconds) for flame onset.
extinction_mechanism: Depressurization venting followed by prototype post-fire smoke scrubber scrub cycle.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Elevated oxygen habitats (26-30% O2) require recalibrating all baseline material flammability certifications (NASA-STD-6001).

name: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G)
hardware_facility: CIR - Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME)
key_phenomenon: Highest oxygen concentration tested in space (up to 85% O2) creating an inside-out spherical cool diffusion flame.
detection_challenge: Inside-out flame geometry isolates hot core; external radiation is minimal until sudden breakthrough.
extinction_mechanism: Radiative dilution extinction when oxidizer flow slowed below critical strain limit.
spacecraft_safety_insight: In hyper-oxygenated systems (such as spacewalk airlocks or pure O2 rovers), gaseous cool flames can form stable spherical envelopes at room temperature.

name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction - Material Ignition (MIST)
key_phenomenon: Opposed-flow flame spread along clear PMMA rods; persistent attachment zone and internal bubble formation.
detection_challenge: Deep subsurface polymer boiling and pyrolysis continues silently beneath a solidified outer char layer.
extinction_mechanism: Extinguishes when flow drops to near zero (<0.5 cm/s); reignites instantly upon flow restoration.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Extinguishing surface fire on space polymers does not eliminate subsurface smoldering risk.

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS-I)
hardware_facility: MSG - SPICE Modular Fan-Driven Flow Duct
investigator: Paul V. Ferkul & Sandra L. Olson
fuel_name: PMMA spheres and flat cast sheets
key_phenomenon: Manual nitrogen gas extinguishant application to burning solid polymer samples.
detection_challenge: Flame envelope flattens against the solid surface under low flow, reducing projected cross-sectional area.
extinction_mechanism: Direct nitrogen extinguisher jet; thermal quench and dilution.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Nitrogen flow must be directed parallel to material surface to dislodge the clinging boundary flame layer.

name: Electric-Field Effects on Microgravity Flames (E-FIELD)
hardware_facility: CIR - Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME)
key_phenomenon: High-voltage DC electric field manipulated charged soot ions, simulating aerodynamic forces and mimicking partial gravity.
detection_challenge: Electric field changes soot agglomeration patterns, shifting optical scattering wavelengths.
extinction_mechanism: Field-induced aerodynamic strain causing localized blow-off.
spacecraft_safety_insight: Novel technology concept: Electrostatic flame deflectors could steer fires away from critical spacecraft electronics.
